Help / Guide

Guidance for all health facility types and for pharmaceutical facilities (Pharmacy and Drug Shop)

About the assessment tool

Each facility type has its own approved checklist, which loads automatically when you select a facility. Most checklists are organized by service area and by the four basic components (4Ps): Practice, Premises, Professional and Product. In the Pharmacy / Drug Shop checklist, the optional Compounding service has no 4P classification.

1. Select the facility

On Self-Assessment, choose the zone, woreda or town, facility type and facility. You can also open Health Facilities and press Assess next to a facility, then choose Self-assessment or Inspection. Closed facilities and regulatory offices are not listed.

2. Complete the checklist

  • Health facilities (hospitals, health centers, clinics, laboratories, health posts and surgery centers): Met = 2 points; Partially Met = 1 point; Unmet = 0 points. The score is the points obtained divided by the maximum points for the answered criteria.
  • Pharmaceutical facilities (Pharmacy and Drug Shop): answer Yes (requirement present) = 1 or No (not present) = 0. The score is the number of Yes answers divided by the number of answered criteria.
  • Optional criteria: Optional criteria are excluded from the mandatory scores and reported separately. A service that contains optional criteria shows a box at the top of that service: tick it only if the facility provides the optional service (or if its optional criteria should be counted); they are then included in the score. In the Pharmacy and Drug Shop checklist, only the Compounding service is optional.
  • Working through the checklist: The checklist is shown one service area at a time. Use the service area list (with the number of answered criteria) or the Previous / Next buttons. Choose All service areas to see everything at once.
  • Criteria with several items to verify: Where a criterion lists several items, answer Yes or No for each item. The criterion result is calculated automatically as in the Excel checklists: all required items Yes = Met; at least half of them Yes = Partially Met; otherwise Unmet. Items marked optional are left out of the calculation.
  • Sign-off: The assessor name, position and signature are required for all submissions. Inspections also require a second inspector name and signature; the facility head name and signature can be added optionally. Self-regulation requires the facility head name and signature.
  • Comments / evidence: Record explanations, evidence and important observations in the comment field of each criterion.
  • Response colours: Met and Yes turn green, Partially Met turns yellow, Unmet and No turn red.
  • Assessment date: Enter the date of the assessment. The system also records, automatically, when the record was created, updated and submitted (device time), and the Dashboard flags back-dated or future-dated entries.
  • Location (GPS): Capturing your current location is mandatory: it must be captured before the checklist can be answered or submitted. The captured location is compared with the registered coordinates of the facility (when the registry has them) and the result is saved with the record. Use a phone with GPS and precise location turned on: laptops often report only an approximate network location that can be far from the real position.
  • Inspection types and scope: Routine and Follow-up inspections (and self-assessments) cover the whole checklist: every mandatory question must be answered before submitting. Concise, Special and Investigative inspections cover only the service area(s) selected on the Inspections page: only those areas must be completed before submitting (use Change scope to adjust a draft).
  • Corrective actions: When a record is submitted, every unmet requirement (No in Yes/No checklists) goes into a corrective action plan. On the Corrective Actions page record the action, the responsible person, the target date and the status.
  • Phones and tablets: The tool works on computers, tablets and smartphones. Use the browser over HTTPS, allow Location and sign with a finger or stylus.
  • Submit and download: Submitting locks the record (Reopen returns it to draft). Use the Download button (Excel or CSV) to download an assessment, and "New assessment" to start another facility.

3. Review service area scores

The Dashboard and Report show the score for each service area and the overall mandatory score. Use them to identify areas that need improvement.

4. Review 4Ps scores

For checklists that classify criteria by 4Ps, the score is also shown for Practice, Premises, Professional and Product.

Understanding the colour categories

Health facilities (Met / Partially Met / Unmet)

  • Red Below 50%.
  • Yellow 50% to 74.9%.
  • Green 75% or above.

Pharmaceutical facilities (Yes / No)

  • Red Below 50%.
  • Yellow 50% to 79.9%.
  • Green 80% or above.

Frequency of self-regulation

  • Conduct full self-regulation at least quarterly.
  • Conduct follow-up inspections according to the facility's action plan.
Important: Checklist-specific instructions and the approved standards take precedence over this guide. The platform is currently a prototype; final scoring and regulatory workflows should be validated before operational use.

User Management

Role-based access control design

RoleAccess scope
Regional AdministratorRegional configuration, user management, and overall oversight
Regional InspectorRegional-level inspections and verification across assigned facilities
Zonal CoordinatorCoordination and monitoring of health facilities within the assigned zone
Woreda / Town CoordinatorCoordination and monitoring of health facilities within the assigned woreda or town
Health Facility ManagerSelf-assessment and reporting for own facility only
Authentication and permissions are illustrative only. This offline prototype does not create real user accounts or enforce production security.

Settings

Prototype configuration

Project name can be changed later without changing the underlying assessment data model.

Interface language: English

Checklists: selected automatically from the facility type

Location (GPS) requirement

Mandatory Location capture is required for every self-assessment and inspection, on computers, tablets and smartphones. The checklist cannot be answered, signed or submitted until the location is captured.

GPS works only when this page is opened from a secure HTTPS website (for example, after publishing to Netlify), not when opened directly as a local HTML file. On a tablet, turn on device Location, allow this website to use location in the browser, and enable Precise location. Phones and tablets with GPS give the most accurate position.
